correctness.rationale: By the finite isometric quotient formula the eccentricity of [p] equals the torus covering radius of {p,-p}. Surjectivity of doubling lets any pair be translated to this form. When r<A/2, the first disk meets each fiber x=x1±r in just one point, so the closed second disk must cover each full fiber. This entails r>=B/2 and puts both fibers in the arc of half-width t=sqrt(r^2-B^2/4) centered horizontally at x2. Since 2t<2r, their shorter circular separation must be A-2r<=2t, which rearranges to r>=R=(A^2+B^2)/(4A); r>=A/2 also implies this. For attainment, the half-diagonal lifts lie in columns spaced A/2 with vertical offsets alternating by B/2. Triangulating each strip using vertical length-B bases and the opposite midpoint-height apex gives the congruent triangles used in RESULT.md; all have circumradius R. The barycentric variance identity covers every triangle by the disks at its vertices, even in the square limiting case. For equality with A>B, the full-fiber arc has its two endpoints forced by A-2R=2t<A/2, giving x2=x1+A/2; for A=B the single opposite fiber requires x2 there because t=0. At x=x1+R-epsilon the second disk misses its vertical antipode for all sufficiently small epsilon>0, while the first disk's arc shrinks to y1. This pins down y2-y1=B/2. The four solutions to 2p=(A/2,B/2) modulo the lattice are two inversion classes, not cone points; translation by (0,B/2) descends to an isometry interchanging them. The frozen script and verification notes were read, not run; their grid does not certify continuum optimality or rigidity. RESULT.md lines 31–115 are the analytic certificate.

value.rationale: Covering radius is a natural intrinsic invariant of a standard singular flat metric, and this problem permits centers anywhere rather than only lattice points or cone points. The complete optimizer locus and uniform transition from the square to arbitrarily elongated rectangles make the result useful, beyond the previously known square radius and attaining pair.
